top_signals.title: Libya Plans New Oil Bidding Rounds Despite Mounting Security Risks
top_signals.summary: Libya has scheduled a bidding round for discovered but undeveloped oil fields in 2027, and another one in 2028 focused on exploration, as it seeks to ramp up oil production despite the unstable security situation. The National Oil Corporation last held a tender for undeveloped oil fields in 2025, the first in 18 years, and last year it awarded five of a total of 22 blocks on offer to companies including Chevron, Eni, Repsol, and QatarEnergy. top_signals.title: Where Soldiers Enjoyed Thanksgiving
top_signals.summary:
Today, I’m slicing turkey. Grease dots my pinks and greens. Scuffs mar my jump boots. As I serve, soldiers feast: smoked turkey, honey-glazed ham, a steamship round of beef, smoked flank steak, and a whole smoked pig. Alongside those entrees, they’re enjoying collard greens, cornbread twice over, baked mac and cheese, shrimp cocktail, deviled eggs, and three gravies. Families of our young soldiers eat for just $8.75. Others, $11.85. The U.S. Army does Thanksgiving well.  While the ideal American Thanksgiving finds everyone back at the family home, I’ve only had four of those in almost 20 years. top_signals.title: One Crew Member Dies as Diesel Tanker Sinks off Ibiza
top_signals.summary: One crew member died as a tanker carrying diesel sank off the coast of Ibiza in the early hours on Thursday, local emergency services and authorities said. The Balearic Islands emergency service has activated an emergency plan after the diesel-carrying vessel sank about 25 nautical miles north of Ibiza, the emergency agency said on Thursday. Seven of the tanker’s 17 crew members were taken to Ibiza, but one of them was pronounced dead later in a hospital, the Balearic Islands emergency service announced. top_signals.title: How does EIA compare different types of energy?
top_signals.summary: To compare production and consumption across different resources, we convert to a common energy metric, British thermal units (Btu), which typically measures the heat content of the fuels such as petroleum, natural gas, and coal that are burned for energy. For energy sources such as hydropower, wind, solar, and geothermal that aren't combusted to create energy, we apply a constant conversion factor based on the heat content of electricity.
